[LERR.9.10] **Where working memory is pre-sized, fault facts have a pool of
their own.** The compiler **must** compute the number of fault-fact sites — one
per `(node, rule)` at which a `ComputationError` can be raised, plus one per
`(node, rule)` at which a `TypeError` can, excluding handlers' ([LERR.9.6]) —
and carry it in the artefact header of every program (RDSC.3.10). It is a
function of the program, not a capacity anyone declares. A runtime that
pre-sizes its working memory **must** allocate exactly that many fault-fact
slots at load, and fault facts **must** use only those slots, never the
working-memory capacity the author or integrator sized. The pool cannot
overflow ([LERR.9.5], [LERR.9.7]), so there is no refusal path. No mode of this
edition pre-sizes working memory ([NRTM.3.1]); the count travels regardless,
so a runtime that does needs nothing more from the artefact.
